english: The set of all real numbers $h$ for which three distinct normals can be drawn to the parabola $y^{2}=4x$ from the point $(h,h-2)$ is the interval $(\alpha,\infty)$. Then the value of $\alpha$ is ______.
hindi: उन सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $h$ का समुच्चय, जिनके लिए बिन्दु $(h,h-2)$ से परवलय $y^{2}=4x$ पर तीन भिन्न अभिलम्ब खींचे जा सकते हैं, अन्तराल $(\alpha,\infty)$ है। तब $\alpha$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Normal $y=-tx+2t+t^{3}$ through $(h,h-2)$; with $u=h-2$: $g(t)=t^{3}-ut-u=0$. Three distinct normals $\iff$ three distinct real roots
solution_full: The normal to $y^{2}=4x$ at $(t^{2},2t)$ is $y=-tx+2t+t^{3}$. It passes through $(h,h-2)$ when $t^{3}+(2-h)t-(h-2)=0$. Put $u=h-2$: $g(t)=t^{3}-ut-u=0$.
Distinct feet give distinct normals (different slopes $-t$), so three distinct normals exist exactly when $g$ has three distinct real roots.
If $u\leq0$: $g'(t)=3t^{2}-u\geq0$, with equality at most at one point, so $g$ is strictly increasing and has exactly one real root.

If $u>0$: $g'(t)=0$ at $t=\pm c$, $c=\sqrt{\dfrac{u}{3}}$; $g$ has a local maximum at $-c$ and a local minimum at $c$. Three distinct real roots $\iff g(-c)>0>g(c)\iff g(c)g(-c)<0$ (since $g(-c)>g(c)$).
At $u=\dfrac{27}{4}$ the cubic has a double root (only two distinct normals). So the condition is $h-2>\dfrac{27}{4}$, i.e. $h>\dfrac{35}{4}$, and $\alpha=\dfrac{35}{4}=8.75$.
originality_note: New: the point moves on a line through (2, 0), the point of the axis where the co-normal cubic degenerates, so the three-normal condition becomes u^2(1 - 4u/27) < 0 with u = h - 2 (way 3, a family of points cut by a condition on a cubic). Closest known: 'points on the axis from which three normals can be drawn (h > 2a)' and the condition 27ak^2 < 4(h - 2a)^3. Different because: both coordinates vary together, so the answer needs the derivative analysis of a cubic with a parameter in two coefficients.

concept_use.Normals to Parabola: Maximum of 3 co-nor: Normals from (h, h - 2) correspond to roots of the co-normal cubic t^3 + (2 - h)t - (h - 2) = 0; three distinct normals need three distinct real roots.
concept_use.Analysis of roots of cubic polynomial wi: The number of real roots of g(t) = t^3 - ut - u is decided from g' (monotonic for u <= 0) and the sign of the product of the extreme values for u > 0.

Checked that the set is exactly (35/4, infinity) (numerical root counts at h = 8.74 and 8.76 give 1 and 3), that the boundary value gives only two distinct normals, and that 8.75 is a positive decimal as planned. Changed: removed a name for the line y = x - 2, which the stem did not need.
key_step: Reducing 'three normals' to three distinct real roots of t^3 - ut - u and using the product of the extreme values.
